notes: FOU-99 v1 iOS — chip-based classifier sourced from the authoritative pocketpal-website APPLE_DEVICES table. Bonsai-1.7B/4B/8B Q1_0 numbers on mid tier are now MEASURED on iPhone 13 Pro (A15) via the Turso submissions table (2026-06-02). Other candidates use the broader Turso iOS dataset top-TG values or extrapolation from Android peers. Major finding: iOS Metal has a Q1_0 kernel fastpath that Android lacks — Bonsai-8B Q1_0 is 4.9× faster on A15 Metal than on A18-Pro-equivalent Android CPU. iOS classifier: utsname.machine → chip → soc_class → tier. ~90 device IDs → 20 chip names → 3 soc_classes → 4 tiers. See _selection_policy for the full membership rule.
_status_note: Classifier (device_id_to_chip, chip_to_class, tier_matrix) is firm — sourced from pocketpal-website/lib/device-lookup.ts. Bonsai-1.7B/4B/8B Q1_0 TG on mid tier is MEASURED on iPhone 13 Pro (A15) via Turso submissions 2026-06-02 (51.2 / 33.0 / 19.9 TG with FA=on, full Metal ngl=99). Bonsai numbers on high/flagship tiers are extrapolated from that A15 anchor using chip-class scaling factors observed in the broader Turso iOS dataset. Other (non-Bonsai) tier candidates use top-TG values from the Turso iOS dataset where present, or extrapolation from the closest-chip Android peer where iOS data is sparse. Full per-chip-class iOS bench campaign still pending.
_quant_policy: On iOS, Metal is the only accelerated backend (no Hexagon HTP). Metal does not give Q4_0 a meaningful PP fastpath over Q4_K_M, so Q4_K_M is primary for Q4 family quants across all tiers. However, Metal DOES have a real Q1_0 fastpath that Android (CPU + Hexagon) lacks — Bonsai-8B Q1_0 runs at ~18 TG on A15 / iPhone 13 Pro vs 4 TG on Android flagship CPU (a 4.4× advantage that grows with model size). This makes Bonsai genuinely useful on iOS as a footprint-AND-speed play, not just a footprint play like on Android. Bonsai variants are listed alongside Q4_K_M throughout.

_selection_policy.rule: Candidate enters tier T iff (Metal TG on rep_device[T] >= tier_floors_metal_tg[T]) AND (peak_load_mem fits ram_band[T] with iOS jetsam margin). Backend is full-offload Metal (ngl=99) — iOS has no equivalent CPU baseline since Metal is universally available. Within a tier, candidates are ORDERED — first per model_id is the primary recommendation. Floor values match Android tier floors (5/8/10/12) so tier semantics stay aligned across platforms; iOS Metal happens to clear these floors more easily than Android CPU does.

_selection_policy._rep_devices_note: Flagship_A rep was changed from 'iPhone 15 Pro / iPhone 17 Pro' to iPhone 17 Pro+ on 2026-06-05 after validation showed iPhone 15 Pro (A17 Pro flagship-class x 8 GiB / 6-8 ram_band) actually classifies as HIGH tier per the matrix, not flagship. The 8-plus ram_band is what brings iPhone 17 Pro (12 GiB) into FLAGSHIP. iPhone 16 Pro (8 GiB A18 Pro) similarly lands in HIGH. Validation against Turso (2026-06-05) shows the matrix routes A17 Pro / A18 Pro 8 GiB devices to HIGH and only the 12 GiB iPhone-Pro / iPad-M-series to FLAGSHIP, which is the correct rep boundary.
_selection_policy.flagship_split_note: iOS 'flagship' is rep-bifurcated: A-Pro iPhones and M-series iPads/Macs differ by ~1.5-2x on 3-4B Q4_K_M Metal (Turso 2026-06-02: A17 Pro ~12, A18 Pro ~10-18, A19 Pro ~13-18 vs M2 ~21-23, M4 ~22-29, M5 ~26). A candidate is admitted to flagship if it clears the floor on flagship_A (the more conservative anchor). Numbers above that floor on M-series only are still listed but should be read as 'works on iPad Pro / Mac, marginal on iPhone Pro'.
_selection_policy.os_killer_margin: iOS jetsam — per-app residency ceiling depends on device class. Empirically: 6 GiB iPhone (e.g. iPhone 13 Pro / A15) loads ~1.7 GiB peak (Bonsai-8B Q1_0) without jetsam, but a Q4_K_M 4B (~2.5 GiB peak) is right at the edge. 8 GiB iPhones tolerate ~3-3.5 GiB peak. M-series iPads with 8-16 GiB tolerate ~6 GiB peak. Used to exclude e.g. Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M on 8 GiB A-Pro iPhones and to keep Bonsai-8B Q1_0 on mid (jetsam-permissible at 1.7 GiB peak even on 6 GiB devices, where Android lowmemorykiller would kill it).

classifier._comment_layer_1: Layer 1: utsname.machine device id → chip name. App reads sysctlbyname('hw.machine') on iOS (returns e.g. 'iPhone16,1') and looks up the chip. Sourced from the curated APPLE_DEVICES table in pocketpal-website/lib/device-lookup.ts (the same identifier-to-marketing-name map used by the benchmarks site). Covers iPhone 8 onward (A11+) and all iPads from iPad mini 5 / Air 3 onward.
classifier._comment_layer_2: Layer 2: chip name → soc_class. Apple chip generations cluster cleanly. A10-A13 are entry by today's LLM-on-mobile standards (≤4 GiB RAM, sub-A15 NE). A14/A15/A16/A18-base are mid (mainline non-Pro of their era, but no Pro-tier cores). A17 Pro / A18 Pro / A19 / A19 Pro / M-series are flagship.
classifier._comment_layer_3: Layer 3: unknown-chip fallback. When utsname.machine isn't in device_id_to_chip (new device released after this rules version), fall back to numeric heuristics on the model identifier. iPhone NN,M with NN ≥ 18 → flagship (we're well into A19+ era); iPad NN,M with NN ≥ 16 + RAM ≥ 8 GiB → flagship. Older unknowns fall back to 'mid' as a safe middle ground.

classifier._comment_matrix: Tier matrix: (ram_band × soc_class) → tier_id. Same 4 output tiers as Android. RAM bands are tighter than Android because iOS reports physicalMemory close to nominal.

low.description: Entry tier — sub-1B models only. iOS anchors (estimated): A12/A13 iPhones with 3-4 GiB RAM (iPhone XR/XS/11/SE 2). _extrapolation_notes.method: Tier values are a mix of measured (from Turso pocketpal-website submissions) and extrapolated. Bonsai 1.7B/4B/8B Q1_0 on mid tier is MEASURED on iPhone 13 Pro (A15, 5.6 GiB) at 51.2 / 33.0 / 19.9 TG with FA=on Metal ngl=99 (community submissions, 2026-06-02). Bonsai on high/flagship is extrapolated by chip-class scaling (×1.4 for A16/A18-base, ×2 for A17 Pro / A18 Pro / A19 / M-series), calibrated to the broader Turso iOS dataset where the same chip-jump factors hold for other model families. Non-Bonsai candidates use top-TG values from Turso where measured (qwen3-0.6b, smollm3-3b, qwen3.5-4b on A18 Pro) or extrapolation from nearest-Android-peer where iOS data is sparse.
_extrapolation_notes.metal_q1_0_advantage_finding: Cross-platform comparison shows iOS Metal has a real Q1_0 kernel fastpath that Android (CPU and Hexagon HTP) lacks. iPhone 13 Pro (A15 mid) Bonsai-8B Q1_0 = 19.9 TG vs Android flagship Myron (A18 Pro-equivalent CPU) Bonsai-8B Q1_0 = 4.07 TG — a 4.9× Metal/CPU advantage that grows with model size (1.7B: 2.0×, 4B: 3.5×, 8B: 4.9×). This makes Bonsai a viable speed+footprint play on iOS where on Android it is footprint-only.
known_limitations: Only one iPhone (iPhone 13 Pro / A15) has measured Bonsai data. A13/A14/A16/A17 Pro / A18 / A19 / M-series Bonsai numbers are extrapolated and need direct measurement.
Q4_K_M vs Q4_0 on Metal has not been measured; policy still prefers Q4_K_M but this should be revisited.
iOS jetsam (per-app memory ceiling) may kill larger models that the rules say fit. Bonsai-8B at 1.7 GiB peak loads on 6 GiB iPhone 13 Pro per user bench — confirmed safe at that RAM tier.

Turso submissions show flash_attn=0 for all six iPhone 13 Pro Bonsai entries even though the user confirms one was FA=ON — iOS bench-submit payload may not capture the flash_attn init setting accurately. Treat flash_attn field on iOS submissions as unreliable.
Mac (macOS) targets are out of scope for this file.
